writerSelfReportIsNotEvidence: each run's `handlers:` line is the shell reporting which handlers it attached. It is carried in runs[] and graded by nothing: a process reporting its own effect is the shape of claim DEF-079 is about. What is graded is the line each handler wrote.
notMeasured: a real stowed exception at 0xC000027B below the managed dispatch boundary - the route DEF-079 was found through. The injected UI fault is an ordinary managed exception in XAML dispatch; nothing on this host can raise the other (DEF-086)

that an UNGUARDED DispatcherQueue callback still reaches no handler - the DEF-085 finding is not re-measured on a normal run. -ProveRed dispatcher is where that state is reproduced, and EFFECT.dispatcher grades the guard rather than the framework

that the ORIGINAL Skills crash of 2026-09-02 took the same path as the stowed exception this lane now raises when armed on dispatcher. What matches is the exception code, the faulting module and the fault offset in WER; nothing here compares stacks (DEF-086)
that a handler fires in a RELEASE build - the injection is compiled out outside DEBUG, so this lane grades the Debug binary only
that the log survives a process kill mid-write - StartupLog appends synchronously per line, which is assumed rather than witnessed here
notes: WER, read out of the Windows Application log after the process was gone: the dispatcher run left NO Application Error. The guard caught the throw, so the process did not fail-fast at 0xC000027B the way the unguarded callback does - which is a second effect of DEF-085's fix, recorded by the operating system rather than by the shell.

EFFECT.dispatcher was an ungraded probe until DEF-085 was fixed: the route reached no handler and the process vanished after `fault: injecting` with nothing appended. It is graded now because the shell guards its own posting sites, so the line it requires is written by this product rather than by the framework. -ProveRed dispatcher removes that guard and reproduces the silence.
